Fine-tune dashboard and config colors here. Edit the default dark and light palettes, or create your own under Custom themes — then click Save colors to apply. Dozens of built-in themes are already available in General → Appearance if you want a ready-made look without editing every color.

config.statsInfoOverviewMsg: A snapshot of your entire bookmark library: how many pages, categories, and bookmarks exist, and how often they are opened on average.
config.statsInfoInsightsMsg: Automated highlights from your library: busiest page, top bookmark, never-opened share, status coverage, and recent activity in the last 48 hours. Links jump to the related section below.
config.statsInfoScoreMsg: A 0–100 score based on library health. Penalties: bookmarks never opened (up to −25), not visited in 90+ days (up to −20), duplicate URLs (up to −15), conflicting shortcuts (up to −10).
config.statsInfoActivityMsg: The sparkline counts bookmarks whose last-open timestamp falls in each bucket — a recency view, not individual opens. The total sums lifetime openCount for bookmarks active in the period (lastOpened within the window). All time uses the last 12 months.
config.statsInfoTopMsg: When a period is selected, only bookmarks opened within that window are listed. Opens shows lifetime openCount, not opens within the period. The bar is relative to the highest value in the list.
config.statsInfoPagesMsg: Bookmark counts per page. With a period filter, only bookmarks opened in that window are included; Opens sums their lifetime openCount. The bar reflects totals relative to the busiest page.
config.statsInfoCategoriesMsg: Bookmark counts per category and page. With a period filter, only bookmarks opened in that window are included; Opens sums their lifetime openCount.
config.statsInfoTagsMsg: Tag coverage across your library. With a period filter, open totals include only bookmarks opened in that window and show lifetime openCount — not opens within the period.
config.statsInfoShortcutsMsg: Coverage bar showing how many bookmarks have a shortcut assigned. The table lists the top 20 shortcuts ranked by open count.
config.statsInfoFindersMsg: Usage stats for custom search finders from the Finders tab. useCount increments when you open a finder from the dashboard.
config.statsInfoRotMsg: 'Never opened' lists bookmarks with zero opens ever. 'Stale' lists bookmarks not opened within the selected period. Use the Health page to archive or remove them.
config.statsInfoConflictsMsg: Duplicate URLs are bookmarks sharing the same address. Shortcut conflicts occur when a shortcut is assigned to more than one bookmark. Use the Health page to resolve them.

config.packedColumnsInfoMessage:

• Reduces empty vertical gaps

• Off: no sync popup noise, but sync still happens
config.allowLocalBookmarksInfoMessage:
When enabled, bookmarks may use http://localhost, 127.0.0.1, and private LAN IPs. Status checks, link previews, auto-heal, and icon downloads from URLs can reach those hosts.

• On by default for local dev workflows
• Turn off if nextDash is exposed on a shared network (SSRF hardening)
config.globalShortcutsInfoMessage:
When enabled, shortcuts from every page can be used anywhere.

• Faster launch across pages
• Higher chance of shortcut conflicts if duplicates exist
config.showBookmarkStatusInfoMessage:
Two levels: this switch enables dashboard status globally. Each bookmark also needs its own status check under Config → Bookmarks.

• Useful for service links, but adds network checks

config.skipFastPingInfoMessage:
Changes how status checks run.

• Off: quick connectivity ping first, then HTTP check
• On: skip quick ping and run HTTP-only check
• Use if fast ping causes false negatives in your setup
config.statusOfflineRetriesInfoMessage:
How many failed ping attempts are needed before a bookmark is marked offline.

• Default: 3
• Range: 1–10
• Higher values reduce false alarms on flaky networks
config.statusOfflineRetryDelayInfoMessage:
Pause between retry pings within one status check.

• Default: 450 ms
• Range: 100–3000 ms
• Only applies while retries are still running
config.statusRecheckIntervalInfoMessage:
How often visible bookmarks are checked again in the background.

• Default: 5 minutes
• Shorter intervals use more network requests

config.showTagCloudButtonInfoMessage: Shows a / button stacked with What's new (desktop). Press / or click to open a tag word cloud (larger = more used). Click or Enter/Space toggles tags in the filter — the modal stays open so you can combine several. Bookmarks match any selected tag (OR). Active tags appear as chips under the title (each with ×) and on the / FAB (#work +1 when multiple). Arrow keys move between tags and Clear tag filter. Escape in the cloud closes the modal; Escape on the dashboard clears all filters. config.configBookmarksTourDemoConsentYesBody: Great — we use random public sites as examples. First: a bookmark in the list and editor (not saved to disk until you click Save).

config.configBookmarksTourEditorDemoFailBody: Open + Bookmark → Add & edit to create a bookmark, then fill name and URL on the right.
config.configBookmarksTourQuickAddBody: Quick add (⚡) saves immediately — unlike Add & edit, no Save click needed.
config.configBookmarksTourQuickAddDoneBody: Quick add writes straight to disk — no Save click. The bookmark appears in the list and on the dashboard.

config.configFindersTourWelcomeBody: Finders are quick-search shortcuts to external sites — Google, DuckDuckGo, Wikipedia, and more. You trigger them from the dashboard with ? plus a shortcut key.
config.configFindersTourConceptBody: Each finder has a name, a search URL with %s as the placeholder for your query, and a one-letter shortcut. nextDash opens the finished URL in your browser — it does not search inside your bookmark list.
config.configFindersTourFieldsBody: Edit each row here: display name, full search URL (must include %s), lowercase shortcut (a–z), and optional comma-separated tags for filtering in config.
config.configFindersTourAddBody: Click + Add finder for a blank row. Change the URL and shortcut to match any search site you use regularly.
config.configFindersTourGoogleIntroBody: A common pattern is Google with URL https://www.google.com/search?q=%s. We prefer shortcut {preferred} if it is free; otherwise we suggest the next available letter. Next we can add this row — only if you agree.
config.configFindersTourGoogleConsentShortcutNo: Shortcut {preferred} is already used by another finder — we will use {shortcut} for this Google example instead.
config.configFindersTourGoogleConsentBody:
We can add a ready-made Google finder to your list now:

• Name: Google
• URL: https://www.google.com/search?q=%s
• Shortcut: {shortcut}

You still need to click Save in config to keep it. Nothing is sent to Google until you use the finder on the dashboard.
config.configFindersTourGoogleNoShortcut: All single-letter shortcuts are already used by finders. Free a letter or remove a finder, then try the tour again.
config.configFindersTourGoogleShortcutTaken: Shortcut {shortcut} was just taken by another finder. Pick a different shortcut manually.
config.configFindersTourGoogleAddedBody: Here is your Google finder. The URL uses %s where your search words go. On the dashboard, press ? then {shortcut} and your query — for example ?{shortcut} nextdash opens Google with that search.
config.configFindersTourGoogleSkippedBody: No problem — you can add finders yourself with + Add finder. Use %s in the URL where the search text should go, and pick a single-letter shortcut.
config.configFindersTourUsageBody: Press ? to open finder mode. Type {shortcut} and your words — e.g. ?{shortcut} nextdash — then Enter. The %s in the URL is replaced with your query. Enable “Include finders in search” under General → Advanced if you also want finders in normal search results.
config.configFindersTourMaintainBody: Drag the ⠿ handle to change order. Remove deletes after confirmation. Usage stats (uses · last used) help you see which finders you actually use.
config.configFindersTourSaveBody: Finder changes are stored when you click Save. If you added the Google example during this tour, save now to keep it after a refresh.

config.configStatsTourWelcomeBody: Below the intro line, this is your stats dashboard: quick links on the left and insight sections on the right. Everything here is read-only — after you save bookmarks or settings elsewhere, reopen this tab to refresh the numbers.
config.configStatsTourIndexBody: Use the quick links on the left to scroll to any block. On wide screens the index stays visible while you read the charts and tables on the right.
config.configStatsTourOverviewBody: Counts for pages, categories, bookmarks, URLs, and shortcuts — plus average opens per bookmark. Click ℹ for a short explanation of each metric.
config.configStatsTourScoreBody: A 0–100 health score with a colour bar. The list below explains penalties: never-opened bookmarks, stale items, duplicate URLs, shortcut conflicts, and more.
config.configStatsTourActivityBody: Lifetime opens for bookmarks active in the period, a count of active bookmarks, and a sparkline of when bookmarks were last opened (not individual opens). Switch week, month, 3 months, 6 months, or all time.
config.configStatsTourTopBody: Tables for most opened and most recently opened bookmarks, with page names and timestamps. Change the period filter to focus on recent usage or all-time leaders.
config.configStatsTourPagesBody: Compare bookmark counts and opens per page, then per category within pages. Use period buttons to limit stats to recent activity or view all time.
config.configStatsTourTagsBody: See tag coverage, unique tags, and which tags appear on the most bookmarks. Tables rank tags and the most opened tagged bookmarks.
config.configStatsTourShortcutsBody: See how many bookmarks have keyboard shortcuts and which shortcuts get the most opens — useful when tuning your search workflow.
config.configStatsTourRotBody: Find bookmarks you never opened, items stale in the chosen period, and recently added links. Tables list candidates to review or remove.
config.configStatsTourConflictsBody: Duplicate URLs and shortcut conflicts are counted here with detail rows. Open Health for deeper triage and one-click fixes on the dashboard.
config.configStatsTourSearchBody: Shows whether the search index is built and how status monitoring is configured. Reopen this tab after changing settings or bookmarks to see updated numbers.
config.configCategoriesTourWelcomeBody: Categories are the columns on your dashboard. Each page has its own list — pick a page, add or rename categories, drag to reorder, and remove ones you no longer need.
config.configCategoriesTourPageBody: Use the Page menu to edit categories for that dashboard page. Switch pages here without leaving the Categories tab.
config.configCategoriesTourAddBody: Click + Add category for a new row. Next we can add a temporary “news” category for practice — only if you agree.
config.configCategoriesTourDemoIntroBody: A short demo helps you see how categories appear on the dashboard. We can create “news” on this page now.
config.configCategoriesTourDemoConsentMessage: For this tour we add a temporary category named “news” on the current page. You will reorder it and remove it before the tour ends — nothing stays on your dashboard.
config.configCategoriesTourDemoAddedBody: Here is your “news” category. Change the name or emoticon anytime. Column order here matches the category tabs on the dashboard.
config.configCategoriesTourDemoSkippedBody: No demo category was added. Use + Add category when you are ready — you can still follow the rest of the tour.
config.configCategoriesTourFieldsBody: Edit the display name and optional two-character emoticon. The category id stays stable when you rename — bookmarks keep their link.
config.configCategoriesTourReorderIntroBody: Drag the ⠿ handle to change order. Next we move “news” to the first slot so you can see the tab shift on the dashboard.
config.configCategoriesTourReorderDoneBody: We moved “news” to the first position — check your dashboard: the category tab order follows this list. Drag the ⠿ handle anytime to change order yourself. Press and hold a category title (~500 ms) to rename it inline.
config.configCategoriesTourRemoveBody: Click Remove (red) on a row to delete that category. You confirm in a dialog; bookmarks can be moved, uncategorized, or deleted depending on your choice.
config.configCategoriesTourRemoveConfirmMessage: Remove the demo category “news” from this page? Bookmarks in it become uncategorized.
config.configCategoriesTourCleanupIntroBody: To leave your library unchanged, we remove the temporary “news” category now. Confirm in the next dialog — same flow as Remove on a normal row.
config.configCategoriesTourCleanupConfirmMessag: We added “news” only for this tour. Remove it now so your categories stay unchanged.
config.configCategoriesTourCleanupDoneBody: The demo category “news” is removed. Your dashboard is back to how it was before the tour.
config.configCategoriesTourCleanupKeptBody: The demo category is still listed. Click Remove on the “news” row and confirm, or restart the tour from General → System tools.
config.configCategoriesTourCleanupNoneBody: There is no demo category left on this page. Use Remove on any row when you want to delete a category — you confirm in a dialog first.

config.configPagesTourWelcomeBody: Pages are separate bookmark workspaces on your dashboard. Each page has its own categories and bookmarks — add pages here, reorder them, and remove ones you no longer need.
config.configPagesTourListBody: Every row is one dashboard page. Drag the ⠿ handle to change tab order on the dashboard. The main page cannot be removed.
config.configPagesTourAddBody: Click + Add page for a new workspace. Next we can add a temporary demo page — only if you agree.
config.configPagesTourDemoIntroBody: A short demo shows how a new page appears on the dashboard. We can create one now.
config.configPagesTourDemoConsentMessage: For this tour we add a temporary page named “Tour demo”. You will see it on the dashboard and remove it before the tour ends — nothing stays behind.
config.configPagesTourDemoAddedBody: Here is your demo page in the list. Rename it anytime — the name is used on the dashboard too.
config.configPagesTourDemoSkippedBody: No demo page was added. Click + Add page when you are ready — you can still follow the rest of the tour.
config.configPagesTourNameBody: Edit the name in the row. It is shown on dashboard page tabs and in Page menus across Config.
config.configPagesTourDashboardIntroBody: New pages show up on the dashboard as tabs and in the Page menu when editing bookmarks. We switch to Bookmarks to point at the same list.
config.configPagesTourDashboardDoneBody: Your new page appears in this Page menu and as a tab on the dashboard (top bar). Switch with 1–9 or Shift+←/→. Click ← back to dashboard to see it live.
config.configPagesTourDashboardSkippedBody: Each page you add shows up here in Bookmarks and as a tab on the dashboard. Use the Page menu to edit bookmarks per page.
config.configPagesTourRemoveBody: Click Remove (red) on a row to delete that page and all its bookmarks. You confirm in a dialog first. The main page cannot be removed.
config.configPagesTourCleanupIntroBody: To leave your library unchanged, we remove the temporary demo page now. Confirm in the next dialog — same flow as Remove on a normal row.
config.configPagesTourCleanupConfirmMessage: We added a temporary page only for this tour. Remove it now so your dashboard stays unchanged.
config.configPagesTourCleanupDoneBody: The demo page is removed. Your dashboard is back to how it was before the tour.
config.configPagesTourCleanupKeptBody: The demo page is still listed. Click Remove on its row and confirm, or restart the tour from General → System tools.
config.configPagesTourCleanupNoneBody: There is no demo page left. Use Remove on any row except the main page when you want to delete a page — you confirm in a dialog first.

config.configCollectionsTourWelcomeBody: Dynamic collections are extra columns on your dashboard. Each collection shows bookmarks that match rules you define — by tag, category, or keyboard shortcut.
config.configCollectionsTourListBody: Saved collections appear here with their match logic (AND / OR) and rule count. Edit or delete any row — bookmarks themselves are never removed.
config.configCollectionsTourAddBody: Click + New collection to open the editor. Next we can pre-fill example rules for tag, category, and shortcut — only if you agree.
config.configCollectionsTourDemoIntroBody: The fastest way to learn is a short demo collection with one rule per field type.
config.configCollectionsTourDemoConsentMessage: We open the editor and add example rules for tag, category, and shortcut (OR logic). You save it for the tour and we remove it before the end — nothing stays on your dashboard.
config.configCollectionsTourDemoOpenedBody: The editor is open with three example rules. Each rule uses Tag, Category, or Shortcut — matching bookmarks appear in this collection on the dashboard.
config.configCollectionsTourDemoSkippedBody: Click + New collection to open the editor. Add rules with the field dropdown: Tag, Category, or Shortcut — then set includes/excludes and a value.
config.configCollectionsTourTagBody: Tag — match bookmarks that have a tag (comma-separated on each bookmark). Example: tag includes “tour-demo”. Values are lowercased when saved.
config.configCollectionsTourCategoryBody: Category — match bookmarks in a category column. Use the category id (same as in Config → Categories), not the display name.
config.configCollectionsTourShortcutBody: Shortcut — match bookmarks with a keyboard shortcut letter. Example: shortcut includes “a”. With OR logic, any matching rule is enough.
config.configCollectionsTourLogicBody: AND requires every rule to match; OR includes bookmarks that match any rule. The demo uses OR so tag, category, or shortcut matches are enough.
config.configCollectionsTourSaveIntroBody: Click Save to store the collection. It appears on the dashboard for the current page when bookmarks match.
config.configCollectionsTourSaveDoneBody: Your demo collection is saved. It appears in the list and on the dashboard as a dynamic column when rules match bookmarks.
config.configCollectionsTourSaveSkippedBody: Click Save in the editor when your rules are ready. Collections are stored in settings and show on the dashboard immediately.
config.configCollectionsTourSaveFailedBody: Fill in a name and at least one rule value, then click Save. Use OR logic so bookmarks matching any rule are included.
config.configCollectionsTourDashboardBody: Open the dashboard — matching collections show as extra columns next to your categories. Hover the column header to see which rules matched.
config.configCollectionsTourCleanupIntroBody: To leave your library unchanged, we remove the temporary demo collection now. Confirm in the next dialog — same as deleting any collection.
config.configCollectionsTourCleanupConfirmMessa: We added a temporary collection only for this tour. Remove it now so your dashboard stays unchanged.
config.configCollectionsTourCleanupDoneBody: The demo collection is removed. Your dashboard is back to how it was before the tour.
config.configCollectionsTourCleanupKeptBody: The demo collection is still listed. Click × on its row and confirm, or restart the tour from General → System tools.
config.configCollectionsTourCleanupNoneBody: There is no demo collection left. Use × on a row to delete a collection — bookmarks are not affected.

config.configThemeTourWelcomeBody: Fine-tune built-in palettes or create custom themes here. This tour adds a temporary demo theme, saves it, activates it on General, then removes it.
config.configThemeTourSubtabsBody: Switch between default dark/light palettes and your own custom themes. We work in Custom themes for this demo.
config.configThemeTourAddIntroBody: Click Add Custom Theme to start from the default starter colors. Next we create one for you automatically.
config.configThemeTourDemoIntroBody: We add a theme named “Tour demo” with a magenta accent so you can spot it in the list and preview.
config.configThemeTourDemoAddedBody: We created “Tour demo” with a distinct accent color. You can rename it in the list — it is saved to disk after the next step.
config.configThemeTourDemoFailedBody: Click Add Custom Theme to create a palette, then continue the tour.
config.configThemeTourPreviewIntroBody: The preview card shows how bookmarks and controls look with your palette. Adjust colors anytime before saving.
config.configThemeTourSaveIntroBody: Save colors writes custom themes to disk so they appear in General → Theme and on the dashboard.
config.configThemeTourSaveDoneBody: Your custom theme is saved. It now appears in General → Appearance. Next we switch there to activate it.
config.configThemeTourSaveFailBody: Click Save colors to write your custom theme to disk before continuing.
config.configThemeTourGeneralIntroBody: Switch to General → Appearance to choose which theme is active across the app.
config.configThemeTourGeneralHandoffBody: Saved themes are picked here under Theme. We pre-select the tour demo so you can see it live on Config and the dashboard.
config.configThemeTourSelectIntroBody: Custom themes appear in this list after you save them on the Theme tab. We apply the tour demo now.
config.configThemeTourSelectDoneBody: “Tour demo” is now your active theme. The dashboard uses it immediately — we remove it at the end of the tour.
config.configThemeTourSelectFailBody: Choose “Tour demo” in the Theme dropdown to apply your new palette.
config.configThemeTourCleanupIntroBody: Remove the temporary theme and restore your previous selection so nothing stays behind.
config.configThemeTourCleanupConfirmMessage: We remove the temporary “Tour demo” theme and restore your previous theme selection.
config.configThemeTourCleanupNoneBody: No demo theme remains. Custom themes you create here are always listed under General → Theme after saving.
config.configThemeTourCleanupDoneBody: The demo theme is removed and your previous theme is restored. Your own custom themes are unchanged.
config.configThemeTourCleanupKeptBody: The demo theme may still be present. Delete it on the Theme tab or restart the tour from General → System tools.
config.configThemeTourCleanupFailBody: Could not remove the demo theme automatically. Delete “Tour demo” in Custom themes on the Theme tab.
config.configTagsTourWelcomeBody: Tags group bookmarks across all pages. Manage them here — add them on each bookmark in the Bookmarks tab (comma-separated).
config.configTagsTourCloudBody: Popular tags appear larger in the cloud. Click a chip to jump to that tag in the list below.
config.configTagsTourListBody: Each row shows how many bookmarks use a tag. Rename merges tags globally; × removes a tag from every bookmark. Click the label to expand the bookmark list.
config.configTagsTourBookmarksIntroBody: Tags are set per bookmark in Config → Bookmarks. Next we can add a sample bookmark and tag it for you — only if you agree.
config.configTagsTourDemoConsentTitle: Try adding a tag on a new bookmark?
config.configTagsTourDemoConsentMessage: We can open the Bookmarks tab, add a temporary bookmark, and set the tag “tour-demo” in the Tags field — then show it here on the Tags tab. The bookmark is removed before the tour ends.
config.configTagsTourBookmarksAddedBody: A new bookmark is open on the right. Tags are comma-separated — we filled in “tour-demo”. Change the field anytime; tags are normalised to lowercase on save.
config.configTagsTourBookmarksFailedBody: Could not add the demo bookmark. Click + Add yourself, select the row, then type tags in the Tags field below.
config.configTagsTourBookmarksSkippedBody: Open + Add to create a bookmark, select it in the list, then type comma-separated tags in the Tags field on the right — for example work, dev, personal.
config.configTagsTourTagsFieldIntroBody: The Tags field lives in the bookmark editor on the right. Comma-separated values become normalised tags when you save.
config.configTagsTourTagsFieldBody: Select a bookmark in the list, then type comma-separated tags here — for example work, dev, personal. Tags are trimmed and lowercased when you save.
config.configTagsTourTagsFieldDoneBody: This Tags field is where you attach labels to a bookmark. We used “tour-demo” — add more with commas. They power search, filters, and dynamic collections.
config.configTagsTourResultIntroBody: Back on the Tags tab: every tag from your bookmarks appears in the cloud and list. We switch here to find your sample tag.
config.configTagsTourResultDoneBody: Here is “tour-demo” in your tag cloud and list. Click a tag to see which bookmarks use it, or rename and delete tags globally.
config.configTagsTourResultEmptyBody: After you save bookmarks with tags, they appear in the cloud and list here. Rename merges tags; delete removes them from every bookmark.
config.configTagsTourCleanupIntroBody: To leave your library unchanged, we remove the temporary bookmark from the Bookmarks tab now.
config.configTagsTourCleanupConfirmMessage: We added a temporary bookmark with tag “tour-demo” for this tour. Remove it now so your library stays unchanged.
config.configTagsTourCleanupDoneBody: The demo bookmark is removed. Your tag list is back to how it was before the tour.
config.configTagsTourCleanupKeptBody: The demo bookmark may still be on the current page in Bookmarks. Delete it there, or restart the tour from General → System tools.
config.configTagsTourCleanupNoneBody: No demo bookmark remains. Tags you add in Bookmarks show up here automatically after save.

  • Recent modal & status rows (v2026.07.05) — rank, recency badge, and open count (D8); status-row hover via shared bookmark-row tokens (D12).

  • Config surface polish (v2026.07.04) — General layer switcher (Essentials / Advanced / Show all in one row); stronger active tab and group styling; list tabs share config-list-tab intro shell; button visibility as divided rows.
  • Bookmarks master/detail (v2026.07.04) — filters and bulk actions above a split view: bookmark list (master) + detail editor (pane) inside one fused surface.
  • Stats split-layout (v2026.07.04) — chip navigation and sidebar index inside one fused Stats surface (Help-style split shell).
  • Theme colors divided list (v2026.07.04) — color rows, custom themes, and preview use divided-list rhythm inside the fused Theme surface (no nested cards).
  • Security & self-hosting (v2026.07.03) — activity log (NEXTDASH_ACTIVITY_LOG), CSP headers, outbound/SSRF rate limits, DNS IP pinning (~2 min), startup validation for PORT and NEXTDASH_DATA_DIR; README, MANUAL, and Help → Security & self-hosting.
  • Extension shortcuts (v2026.07.03) — optional shortcut when saving a tab; auto-suggest from bookmark name; 409 when taken on that page.
  • Dashboard sync (v2026.07.03) — hash-based GET /api/data-revision; stale cache detects name, URL, shortcut, tags, and category; preview metadata cache flushes periodically; shared cache-bust tokens across pages.
  • What's new modal (v2026.07.03) — scroll to load up to the 7 most recent releases (lazy per-version JSON).
  • General layer scroll (v2026.07.03) — Essentials/Advanced toggle preserves the General layer toolbar viewport position when scroll is within both layers.
  • Playwright E2E (v2026.07.03) — full test suite green with isolated temp data; config, tags, finders, and layout-nudge tests aligned with current behaviour.
  • Bookmark category sync (v2026.07.02) — new bookmarks and category changes appear in the correct dashboard column right away; GET /api/data-revision keeps open tabs in sync after saves and server restarts.
  • Bookmark tag sync (v2026.07.02) — tag edits re-render smart collections and the tag-filter view; stale-cache detection includes tags.
  • Config polish (v2026.07.02) — Stats guided tour re-enabled; General spacing (B6), shared tab intro (B7), uniform label width (A8), keyboard row rhythm (A10), persistent empty hints on list tabs (B11), broader prefers-reduced-motion (C15).
  • Inline edit focus (v2026.07.01.8) — long-press inline editor uses a nearly opaque panel and tour-like full-page blur so labels and fields stay readable on glass and launcher layouts.
  • Config polish continued (v2026.07.01.8) — unsaved dot on Extras ● when only Collections changes (C14); broader prefers-reduced-motion coverage for tag cloud, keyboard pulse, health shimmer, and settings-search promo (C15).
  • Config surface polish (v2026.07.01.5) — Bookmarks Context panel and Collections editor fused into config-tab-surface cards (B4/B8). List tabs share config-list-tab shell; Finders uses the shared filter field (A2/A6). Empty states use hidden (B11). Breadcrumb shows Tags filter, Stats period, and Collections edit context (B14). General Tours & onboarding uses grouped action rows (A10/B6). Skip tour always marks the tour completed on the server so it never auto-starts again. Health redirect check no longer freezes the app; title fetch and Retest all UX improved.
  • Config polish (v2026.07.01.4) — Pages and Categories tabs match Tags with a Usage column (popularity bar + bookmark count). Help tab uses the shared config-tab-surface shell (intro + filter toolbar + fused index/content). Unsaved changes show a dot on the tab group label (e.g. System ●). Config tab chrome respects prefers-reduced-motion. Stats guided tour paused until re-enabled.
  • Config surface parity (v2026.07.01.1) — Classic briefly fused header + save row + tabs in v2026.07.01.1 (C10, reverted in v2026.07.01.3); Classic now keeps configuration header separate from save row and grouped tabs (Modern/Glass still unified). Keyboard, Bookmarks, Stats, and Backups tabs use the shared config-tab-surface list-shell: toolbar + content in one card with divided rows. Stats moves Refresh/Export CSV into the in-surface filter toolbar. Health links show a compact count-only badge pill (broken count takes priority). Dismissed discoverability promos and What's new progress sync via settings.discoverabilityState in settings.json across browsers. Inline bookmark editor regression fixed (form stays interactive during long-press edit). Modern/Glass hotfix: keyboard-selected bookmarks use full-row highlight again (not border-only).
  • Config tab bar v5 (v2026.07.01) — tabs grouped as System, Dashboard, Extras, and Help (Keyboard in System). Compact save strip with save-mode pill, Undo/Discard only when dirty, and a scroll hint when tabs overflow. Modern/Glass: header + save row + tabs fuse into one chrome card; list tabs use one fused surface; Classic keeps configuration header separate from save row and grouped tabs (v2026.07.01.3). Group widths scale with tab count; ←/→ cross groups, Alt+←/→ jumps between groups. Compact breadcrumb tab › context. Documented on cheat sheet and Config → Keyboard.
  • Config Tab Consistency (v2026.06.31) — shared intro, toolbar, filter, and empty-state layout across list tabs; on Classic layout, toolbar + list fuse into one surface card. Breadcrumb shows tab context (page/category on Bookmarks and Categories) and save mode (Requires save, Auto-save, Read-only). One save status line beside Save replaces the old unsaved badge. Config → Bookmarks: collapsible Context panel (replaces Structure) switches page/category only — reorder, archive, merge on Pages/Categories tabs; open/closed state remembered. Opening /config#bookmarks on a phone shows a desktop-only card. Intro spacing and toolbar clipping fixes; guided tours still lock the rest of the page.
  • Per-category sort, category titles, favicons & pin/note polish (v2026.06.28) — each category header has A–Z and Rec sort chips at full visibility with a clear active state on the current mode (including Other and unknown-category blocks); global sort removed from Config → General; legacy sortMethod migrates on all pages at once; :sort targets the focused category and shows its name in the palette. Long category names shrink down to the xs minimum and may wrap to two lines while sort chips stay on the first row. Press and hold a category title (~500 ms, not on sort chips) to rename inline — double-click still works. Dashboard feature tour steps highlight finders, commands, and search via a body-level focus ring (Safari stacking fix). First category rename shows a one-time Got it promo; Esc dismisses the promo and cancels rename. Config → General → Bookmarks: Show favicons (:favicons on/off); incremental row refresh picks up favicon visibility via data-render-fp. Pin/note row icons removed; pins still sort to the top and notes stay searchable. Smart-collection ℹ popover fixed.

config.helpPageTipsIntro: On the dashboard, a single shortcut hint can rotate above the footer when you enable Show tips above buttons under General → Dashboard (off by default, or turn on with :tips on). The full catalogue lives here if you want to read ahead — collapsed by default so the help page stays scannable.
config.helpPageTroubleshootFooter: Found a bug or have feedback? Visit the GitHub repository to report issues or suggest improvements.
config.bookmarkDashboardPreviewHint: Hover to see the full tile
config.bookmarkLinkPreviewEmpty: No preview metadata yet — refresh to fetch title, description and image.
config.bookmarkPreviewMaintenanceHint: Refresh or clear title, description and image stored on bookmarks for hover cards and tooltips on the dashboard.
config.bookmarkPreviewMaintenanceInfoMessage:
Each bookmark can store link preview data (title, description, image) used for hover cards and tooltips on the dashboard.

• Refresh all — re-fetches metadata for every bookmark with a URL (may take a while)
• Clear all — removes stored metadata and the server preview cache; previews are fetched again on next hover
• Per-bookmark refresh/clear is also available in Config → Bookmarks
config.bookmarkPreviewRefreshAllConfirmMessage: Re-fetches title, description and image for every bookmark with a URL. This may take a while for large libraries.
config.bookmarkPreviewClearAllConfirmMessage: Removes stored preview title, description and image from every bookmark and clears the server preview cache. Hover cards will fetch again on next use.
config.bookmarksTabIntro: Browse and edit all bookmarks in a split view: list on the left, detail panel on the right. Filter by page or category, use bulk actions, or expand Context to switch page and category while you edit.
config.bookmarksPhoneBlockLead: Bookmark editor needs a wider screen
config.bookmarksPhoneBlockHint: On your phone you can add and edit bookmarks from the dashboard (+ Bookmark). Open config on a tablet or computer for the full split-view editor, context panel, and bulk actions.
config.categoriesIntro:
Categories organise bookmarks within a page. Select a page to manage its categories.
Drag the ⠿ handle to reorder (saves automatically). Merge combines two categories and moves their bookmarks. On the Bookmarks tab, the Context panel only switches the active category filter.
config.collectionsTabIntro: Dynamic collections appear on the dashboard and show bookmarks matching the rules you define.
config.collectionsEmptyHint: No collections yet. Create one to group bookmarks by tag, category, or shortcut.
config.categoriesListEmptyHint: No categories on this page yet. Add one to organise bookmarks.
config.categoriesMobileOnlyDesktop: Category management is available on desktop. Open config on a larger screen to add or reorder categories.
config.categoryNameMustBeUnique: Category name must be unique and not empty.
config.mergeCategoryImpact: {count} bookmarks will move to the target category.
config.findersIntro: A finder is a shortcut to a search engine. Set a search URL with %s where your query should go (e.g. https://www.google.com/search?q=%s), pick a short letter shortcut, and on the dashboard type ? plus that shortcut and your words — e.g. ?du linux opens DuckDuckGo with “linux” in your browser.
config.pagesIntro:
Pages group your bookmarks. Each page has its own set of categories and bookmarks on the dashboard.
Drag the ⠿ handle to reorder pages (saves automatically). Use Archive to hide a page without deleting its bookmarks. Double-click a page tab on the dashboard to rename it. On the Bookmarks tab, the Context panel only switches the active page.
config.pagesMobileOnlyDesktop: Page management is available on desktop. Open config on a larger screen to add or reorder pages.
config.dashboardSyncFailed: Dashboard sync failed. Retry from config.
config.tagsTabIntro: Manage tags across all bookmarks. Rename or delete tags globally, or see which bookmarks carry each tag. Changes save automatically.
config.tagsListEmptyHint: No tags yet. Add tags to bookmarks via the Bookmarks tab or the inline editor on the dashboard.
config.tagsMobileOnlyDesktop: Tag management is available on desktop. Open config on a larger screen to rename, merge, or delete tags.
config.tagMergeMessage: Tag "{new}" already exists on {count} bookmarks. Merge "{old}" into it?
config.tagDeleteMessage: Removes the tag from {count} bookmarks. Bookmarks are kept.
config.featureTourHint: Start the interactive tour: learn search, finders, commands and key settings.
config.themeInfoMessage:
Chooses the colour theme for the dashboard and config.

• Includes built-in dark/light and any custom themes from Config → theme
• Saved when you click Save in config
config.autoDarkModeInfoMessage:
Automatically switches between light and dark theme based on your system preference.

• Only works with built-in themes that have dark and light variants
• Not available with custom themes — those use one fixed palette
• Useful on laptops and phones that follow OS appearance
config.autoDarkModeUnavailableHint: Not available with custom themes. Custom themes use one fixed palette instead of separate dark and light variants. Select a built-in theme to enable auto dark mode.
config.systemAppearanceHintActive: Auto dark mode is on — the dashboard theme follows this system appearance.
config.systemAppearanceHintIdle: Your OS appearance right now. Enable auto dark mode to switch themes when this changes.
config.systemAppearanceHintUnsupported: System appearance shown for reference. Auto dark mode needs a built-in dark/light theme pair — not available with custom themes.
config.backgroundPickerInfoMessage:
Optional wallpaper behind the bookmark grid.

• None: plain theme background
• Auto: gradient matched to the active theme
• Gradient / Image: pick a preset or paste an image URL
• Opacity slider controls how strong it appears
config.backgroundOpacityInfoMessage:
How visible the background is (65–100%).

• Lower values keep bookmarks easier to read
• Applies to gradient and image backgrounds
config.showBackgroundDotsInfoMessage:
Subtle dot pattern on the dashboard background.

• Purely decorative
• Turn off for a cleaner look
config.enableAnimationsInfoMessage:
UI transitions and motion effects.

• On: smoother category collapse, modals, etc.
• Off: snappier feel, can help on slower devices
config.fontPresetInfoMessage:
Font family for the whole interface.

• Mono fonts suit the terminal aesthetic
• Sans fonts are easier for long reading
• Upload a custom font below — it appears as an option in this dropdown and stays available when you switch presets
config.fontSizeInfoMessage:
Global text scale from xs to xl.

• Affects bookmarks, config, and search
• Combine with density for tighter layouts
config.fontWeightInfoMessage:
How bold body text appears.

• Normal is default
• Semi-bold / bold increase contrast on dense screens
config.iconStylingInfoMessage:
Tints bookmark favicons to match the active theme.

• Muted / Tinted / Overlay styles
• Intensity slider controls strength
• Preview shows sample icons
config.columnsInfoMessage:
How many bookmark tiles fit on one row (1–6).

• Wider screens often suit 3–4
• Launcher layout may ignore this
config.layoutVersionInfoMessage:
Switch between classic, modern, and glass dashboard styling.

• Classic: stable, recommended — current look, unchanged
• Modern: early beta — refreshed visuals, same structure; still in development
• Glass: early beta — translucent surfaces with blur; still in development
• Themes still control all colors

Modern and Glass are not finished yet. Use Classic for the best experience.
config.layoutVersionBetaNotice: Modern and Glass are still in early beta and not finished yet. Classic is recommended for the best experience.
config.layoutPresetInfoMessage:
Overall bookmark grid style.

• Default, Compact, Cards, Masonry, List, Launcher, etc.
• Each changes spacing, card shape, and row height
config.densityModeInfoMessage:
Spacing between tiles and text size within the preset.

• Comfortable → Dense → Auto
• Auto adapts to screen size and zoom
config.showDashboardTitleInfoMessage:
Shows the nextDash title (or custom title) at the top.

• Off: more vertical space for bookmarks
config.launcherIconSizeInfoMessage:
Icon scale when using the Launcher layout preset.

• Only applies in Launcher mode
config.calendarUrlInfoMessage:
Link opened when you use the calendar shortcut from the date line.

config.showIconsInfoMessage:
Shows favicons on each bookmark.

• Fetched automatically when adding links
• Can be refreshed from config → bookmarks
config.showShortcutsInfoMessage:
Displays keyboard shortcut labels on tiles.

• Used with / or letter search depending on search mode
• Global shortcuts setting affects cross-page use
config.showPinIconInfoMessage:
Small pin marker on pinned bookmarks.

• Pin via command :pin or inline edit
config.showNoteIconInfoMessage:
Indicator when a bookmark has a note.

• Notes are edited with :note or inline edit
config.showLinkPreviewCardsInfoMessage:
Hover card with title/description preview for a bookmark.

• Only on keyboard focus or hover

config.linkPreviewHoverDelayInfoMessage:
How long to wait before showing the preview card.

config.bookmarkSortingInfoMessage:
Default order for bookmarks on each page.

• A–Z, Recently used, Pinned first
config.openLinksInNewTabInfoMessage:

config.pasteUrlQuickAddInfoMessage:

config.languageInfoMessage:
Interface language for dashboard, config, and modals.

config.showDateInfoMessage:

config.dateFormatInfoMessage:

config.showTimeInfoMessage:
Clock in the dashboard header.

config.showWeatherWithDateInfoMessage:

config.weatherSourceInfoMessage:

config.weatherLocationInfoMessage:
City or place name for manual weather lookup.

config.weatherUnitInfoMessage: Celsius or Fahrenheit for displayed temperature.
config.weatherRefreshInfoMessage:
How often to fetch new weather data.

config.enableSmartCollectionsInfoMessage:
Automatic categories such as Today, Recently opened, or Stale.

config.buttonBarPositionInfoMessage:

config.showDockLayoutSelectorInfoMessage:

config.colorizeStatusInfoMessage:

config.showStatusLoadingInfoMessage:

config.deviceSpecificSettingsInfoMessage:

config.enableCustomFaviconInfoMessage:

config.enableCustomTitleInfoMessage:

config.helpPageQuickStartBody:
If you only have half a minute, start here. Open search with >, type part of a bookmark name, and press Enter to open it. Press + when you want the full new-bookmark form, or & on the dashboard for a one-line quick add (name | url | shortcut). Recent bookmarks are always one key away with *, and the keyboard cheat sheet is under ! or F1.

Most layout and behaviour lives under config → General. On desktop, Ctrl+Shift+K finds any setting or help section, while Ctrl+K runs quick actions such as adding a page or refreshing favicons. The ℹ buttons beside individual settings explain what each toggle does without leaving the form.
config.helpPageOnboardingBody:
The first time you open nextDash, a short onboarding wizard helps you pick language, how links open, whether you want date and weather in the header, how search should feel, and how bookmarks respond to keyboard and mouse. You can switch language while the wizard is open, skip any step, or finish later — nothing is locked in until you save in config.

When you start with an empty library, the last steps invite you to create pages and add a first bookmark so the dashboard is useful immediately. After onboarding you may see a one-time What's new summary or a few gentle spotlights (paste URL, preview cards, layout versions). Those are optional nudges, not extra wizards.
config.helpPageConfigGeneralBody:
General is the control room for the whole dashboard. The toolbar at the top of the tab switches between Essentials (everyday choices), Advanced (fine-grained power settings), and All sections (everything on one scrollable page). Essentials covers language, theme, fonts, layout, bookmark display, smart collections, and which footer buttons appear. Advanced adds background tuning, status monitoring, branding, search behaviour, and system tools grouped into cards you can expand or collapse.

Within the bookmark card, display options (icons, shortcuts, badges, link preview) sit above a divider, with behaviour options (sorting, tabs, page names) below — so you can see at a glance what changes how tiles look versus how they act. Tours and onboarding resets live under Advanced → System in a collapsible block if you want to replay a guided tour.

Changes in General do not apply until you press Save. When you do, the dashboard refreshes in place without a full page reload, so you can tweak, save, and immediately see the result.
config.helpPageConfigTabsBody:
Config tabs are grouped so related work stays together. On desktop you will see System (General, Theme, Backups, Stats, Keyboard), Dashboard (Pages, Categories, Bookmarks), Extras (Tags, Finders, Collections), and Help. Group labels sit above the tabs; the active group is highlighted so you always know which area you are in.

When a tab in a group has unsaved changes, a dot appears on the group label — for example System ● while General is dirty. The breadcrumb under the tabs shows a compact path such as General › Layout. The save row at the top tells you whether the current tab needs an explicit save or auto-saves (Collections and Finders save on their own).

On a phone, the tab bar collapses into a simpler set; wide tablets keep the desktop grouping. Keyboard shortcut reference lives in Help → Keyboard shortcuts and in the Keyboard tab under System.
config.helpPageNavigationBody:
nextDash is built for keyboard-first browsing once you learn a handful of keys. Number keys 1–9 jump to pages (when search is closed) and select the first visible bookmark on the new page. Press , for a page overview with counts, navigate with arrows, and confirm with Enter. Move between pages with Shift+← / Shift+→ — plain arrow keys move within the bookmark grid, not across pages.

Start grid navigation with Tab, a click, G followed by a digit, or the first arrow key; then ↑/↓ and ←/→ move the highlight. Enter or Space opens the selected bookmark; Esc clears selection or cancels an unsaved drag reorder. On Mac, Cmd+C copies the highlighted URL. Collapsed categories and items hidden by search are skipped automatically so the highlight never lands on invisible rows.
config.helpPageMobileBody:
On narrow screens, portrait tablets, or touch-first devices, nextDash switches to a lighter chrome so the essentials stay reachable. A short banner on dashboard and config explains what changed; you can dismiss it once you know the layout.

On phones the dashboard footer keeps Search and + Bookmark; commands and finders live inside the search overlay via the >, :, and ? tabs. Recent bookmarks are available through command mode (:open recent or * with a hardware keyboard). The cheat sheet and some footer buttons are desktop-only. Config on a phone focuses on the settings you are most likely to need on the go; the full split-view bookmark editor expects a wider window.
config.helpPageKeyboardBody: Most dashboard keys can be rebound under Config → Keyboard. Open the cheat sheet on the dashboard with ! or F1 for a searchable list of defaults. With a bookmark row selected, Shift+M moves it, Shift+T opens quick-tag, and Shift+D deletes with undo in the toast. Home, End, and Page Up/Page Down jump larger distances through the grid — see Navigation above for page-level keys.
config.helpPageBookmarksDashboardBody:
On the dashboard, bookmarks behave like a small spreadsheet: arrow keys move the selection, ; opens inline edit on the highlighted row, and long-press on the row (not the left drag strip) opens the same editor with touch. The narrow left strip is only for dragging — reorder inside a category or drop into another column.

While inline edit is open, grid navigation pauses so you do not accidentally jump away. Hovering a bookmark can load a rich preview when link preview is enabled in General. Edits to smart-collection rows update the real bookmark everywhere it appears, so tags and notes stay consistent.
config.helpPageSearchBody:
Search is really three modes behind one overlay: > for normal search, : for commands, and ? for finders. Typing : alone opens grouped commands (bookmarks, navigation, layout, smart collections, settings); recent commands float to the top when you reopen it. Filters such as tag:work, category:news, status:online, and page:2 narrow results without changing the dashboard layout.

On desktop, / opens the tag word cloud when that button is enabled; otherwise it follows your fuzzy search setting. Commands like :layout, :density, and :tips on change the UI in place. Turn on Keep search open when empty if you hop in and out of search all day.
config.helpPageDateWeatherBody:
The header can show date, time, and optional weather as a quiet clock line above your bookmarks. Date and time can be toggled independently, with formats ranging from compact numeric styles to weekday-only or long weekday labels. Time supports 24-hour or 12-hour clocks.

When weather is enabled, choose browser geolocation or a manual city, pick Celsius or Fahrenheit, and set how often forecasts refresh. A small icon reflects the current condition. If weather does not appear, check that a location is set and save once — the line renders below date/time when both are active.
config.helpPageSmartBody:
Smart collections are automatic groups such as Today, Recently opened, Stale bookmarks, and Most used. Each can be turned on or off per page and limited to a maximum number of items (use 0 for unlimited). They appear alongside ordinary categories and can be collapsed like any other section.

Enable Tag collections under General → Smart Collections to spawn one dynamic group per tag, with an optional minimum bookmark count so rare tags do not clutter the dashboard.
config.helpPageTagsBody:
Tags are free-form labels you add in config or inline on the dashboard. They are normalised on save (trimmed, lowercased, deduplicated). In search, tag:work filters overlay results without rearranging the grid. On desktop, the tag cloud (/ or the FAB) lets you toggle multiple tags while the modal stays open; matching bookmarks need any selected tag.

Tag collections turn heavily used tags into first-class dashboard sections. Command mode :tag work lists matching bookmarks in the palette only, which is useful when you want a quick list without changing the home view.
config.helpPageCollectionsBody:
Custom collections are rule-based groups you define under Config → Collections. Each has a name, optional emoji icon, match logic (AND or OR), and one or more rules on tag, category, or shortcut. Matching bookmarks appear as read-only sections on the dashboard, sorted with smart collections before ordinary categories.

Collections save immediately — no main Save button required. An optional guided tour walks through creating a demo collection, previewing it on the dashboard, and cleaning up afterward; replay it from System & tools if you want a refresher.
config.helpPageSortingBody:
Pinned bookmarks always float to the top of their category and sort alphabetically among themselves; everyone else follows the category sort mode (manual drag, A–Z, or recent). Click A–Z or Rec in a category header to switch modes; drag handles hide while automatic sort is active.

Categories can be collapsed and renamed with a long press on the header (avoid the sort buttons). Drag the ⠿ grip on a category title to reorder categories on the dashboard; the same order can be edited in config → Categories with drag or arrow keys. Command palette :sort applies to the focused category when you prefer keyboard control.
config.helpPageManageBody:
The config workspace is where pages, categories, and bookmarks are edited in bulk. The Bookmarks tab uses a split view: a filterable list on the left and a detail editor on the right, with an optional Context panel to switch page and category without leaving the tab. Desktop users can press Ctrl+Shift+K to jump to any setting and Ctrl+K for quick actions.

Each bookmark supports name, URL, page, category, shortcut, icon, tags, notes, pin state, and optional status checks. Bulk select supports move, pin toggle, delete, and favicon refresh. Conflict highlighting warns about duplicate URLs or shortcuts before you save. Guided tours for Pages, Categories, Bookmarks, Stats, and Finders replay from Advanced → System when you want a walkthrough again.
config.helpPageFindersBody:
Finders are search shortcuts that send a query to an external site — for example ?g your terms for Google. Define them under Config → Finders with a shortcut letter and a URL containing %s where the query belongs. Reorder with drag or arrow keys; duplicates are flagged before save.

When Include finders in search is on, a bookmark and a finder with the same shortcut both appear in results. A guided tour on first visit can add a sample Google finder; replay it from System & tools anytime.
config.helpPageStatusBody: Status monitoring optionally pings bookmarks to show online/offline state. Enable it under General → Advanced → Status, choose whether to show ping detail and a loading spinner, and use Skip fast ping check if background noise is too high. For deeper triage, open the /health page to repair broken links, refresh titles, or archive stale entries.
config.helpPageHealthBody:
The health page is a dedicated triage desk for your whole library. Summary cards show totals for healthy, broken, duplicate, stale, and unchecked bookmarks; click a card to filter the list. Search, page filters, and bulk actions (retest, open all broken, merge duplicates) sit in one compact toolbar.

Each row exposes favicon refresh, health score, and repair actions such as re-check status, detect redirect, refresh title, or archive. Keyboard j/k or arrows move focus; O opens the URL; Enter jumps to the bookmark in config. Layout and theme follow your dashboard settings so the page feels familiar.
config.helpPageBackupBody:
Backups live under Config → Backups. A ZIP export includes pages, bookmarks, categories, finders, settings, and themes — import replaces everything, so export first. From the dashboard, :backup opens the backups tab and :export downloads immediately.

You can also import browser HTML exports (folders become categories; duplicate URLs are skipped) or export all bookmarks to CSV for spreadsheets. A preview before browser import shows how many pages and bookmarks will arrive.
config.helpPageBrandingBody:
Appearance starts under Essentials → Layout: pick Classic, Modern, or Glass (same structure, different polish), then density, columns, and dashboard title. Advanced → Appearance handles background images, UI font (including an uploaded custom font), and favicon harmonisation. Auto dark mode follows the system theme.

Theme colours are edited on the Theme tab with live preview, packaged palettes, JSON import/export, and per-session undo. Custom favicons upload under Advanced → Branding. Switch layout version from the dashboard with :layoutversion if you want to experiment before saving.
config.helpPageDataBody:
Server data lives in ./data by default (override with NEXTDASH_DATA_DIR for Docker volumes or multiple instances). Open dashboard tabs poll a revision endpoint so bookmark grids refresh when another tab saves changes.

Device-specific settings can be stored in browser local storage when enabled, which lets one computer keep different visual preferences than another. Link preview metadata is cached on the server and flushed periodically to keep hover cards snappy.
config.helpPageExtensionBody:
The browser extension in the extension/ folder saves the current tab to nextDash. Install it unpacked in Chrome, set the server URL, and paste the write token if your server uses NEXTDASH_WRITE_TOKEN. The save form supports optional shortcut (auto-suggested from the title), tags, and notes, with duplicate URL warnings before you commit.

If CORS is restricted, add your chrome-extension:// origin to NEXTDASH_CORS_ORIGINS. After a successful save you can jump straight into nextDash; an open dashboard on the same host may toast and refresh automatically.
config.helpPageSecurityBody:
nextDash has no built-in user accounts — anyone who can reach the URL can read and write data unless you protect it with a VPN, private network, or reverse-proxy authentication. Do not expose plain HTTP to the public internet.

Set NEXTDASH_WRITE_TOKEN so write APIs require the X-NextDash-Token header (pages inject it for same-origin use). Restrict CORS with NEXTDASH_CORS_ORIGINS when using the extension. Outbound fetches validate public IPs to reduce SSRF risk; tune rate limits and activity logging with the environment variables documented in the README security section.
config.helpPageTroubleshootBody:
If bookmarks disappear, check the page selector and category filter in config — an empty page looks like data loss but is usually a filter. Sorting surprises usually mean a category is in A–Z or Recent mode instead of manual order, or pins are doing their job. When tips never show, enable Show tips above buttons under General → Dashboard.

Search gaps often clear up with fuzzy mode or filters like tag:work. Collections that never appear need at least one rule with a value; tag collections need enough tagged bookmarks to meet the minimum. Extension save failures almost always trace to server URL, write token, or CORS. API 401 means a missing token; 429 means rate limits — wait or raise the configured limits.

colors.title: theme customization
colors.importSuccess: Theme imported — click Save colors to persist.
colors.invalidColorValue: Fix invalid color values before saving.
colors.contrastWarning: Low contrast between primary text and background ({ratio}:1).
colors.builtinTabHint: Edit packaged theme palettes (Cherry Graphite, Nordic Frost, etc.). Activate a theme under General → Appearance, then Save in the config header.
colors.mobileReadonlyBanner: Theme editing needs a wider screen. You can preview palettes here; open config on desktop to edit and save.
colors.resetColorsMessage: Are you sure you want to reset all DEFAULT colors (dark/light) to default values? This action cannot be undone.
colors.customTabHint: Use Add Custom Theme to create a palette from the default starter colors.
colors.defaultDarkHint: Edits the default dark palette used when classic dark themes are active.
colors.defaultLightHint: Edits the default light palette used when classic light themes are active.
colors.palettesInfoMessage:
Three ways to edit colors on this tab:

• Dark and Light — change the fallback palettes for the classic dark/light themes in General → Appearance.

• Custom themes — create your own single-palette themes with Add Custom Theme. Each custom theme is one fixed look, not a day/night pair.

• Built-in named themes (Cherry Graphite, Nordic Frost, etc.) are picked in General → Appearance. Their packaged colors live in the server defaults unless you override palettes here.
colors.saveColorsInfoMessage:
Two separate save actions:

• Save colors (this tab) — writes palette edits from the Theme tab to the server. Use this after changing hex values or adding/removing custom themes.

• Save (config header) — stores General settings: which theme is active, layout, bookmarks, language, etc. It does not save color hex values from this tab.

Typical flow: edit colors → Save colors → pick the theme under General → Appearance → Save in the header.
colors.customThemesInfoMessage:
Custom themes are single palettes you create here.

• Add Custom Theme clones the default starter colors. Rename the theme and adjust colors in the editor on the right.

• To use it on the dashboard, select it under General → Appearance and click Save in the config header.

• Auto dark mode (General → Appearance) only works with built-in themes that have separate dark and light variants. It is disabled while a custom theme is selected — custom themes do not switch with your system appearance.

onboarding.welcomeBody: Quick setup in a few clicks. You can skip anytime.
onboarding.mobileWelcomeBody: Quick mobile setup — language and theme. Full settings are available on a computer or tablet.
onboarding.mobileLanguageThemeBody: Pick your language and dashboard theme.
onboarding.mobileFinishBody: Use search to open bookmarks. Swipe left or right to switch pages. Open config on a computer for full settings.
onboarding.languageStepBody: Pick your language and how links open.
onboarding.weatherLayoutStepBody: Choose weather display and tight columns behavior.
onboarding.weatherStepBody: Choose weather display and tight columns behavior.
onboarding.layoutStepBody: Choose classic, modern, or glass dashboard styling. Same structure — only visuals change.
onboarding.layoutStepOptional: Optional — change anytime in config → General → Layout.
onboarding.layoutStepHint: Modern refreshes spacing and surfaces; glass adds translucent blur; classic keeps the original look.
onboarding.tightColumnsHint: Tight columns fill vertical space better with many categories. Off keeps classic flow.
onboarding.searchTipsStepBody: Tune keyboard flow and footer hints.
onboarding.collectionsStepBody: nextDash can auto-group your bookmarks into dynamic sections. Enable the ones that suit your workflow — you can tweak them anytime in config.
onboarding.collectionsShowTodayHint: Shows bookmarks that match your time of day — work tools in the morning, leisure in the evening.
onboarding.collectionsShowMostUsedHint: Shows your most opened bookmarks at a glance.
onboarding.statusMonitorStepBody: Status checks ping selected bookmarks in the background and show online/offline on each row.
onboarding.statusMonitorStepBodyEmpty: When you add bookmarks, enable status per row to see online/offline indicators. GitHub is a good example to try first.
onboarding.statusMonitorStepOptional: Optional — skip or change anytime in config or on the health page.
onboarding.statusMonitorAllPagesNote: Bookmarks from all pages — enable more per bookmark in config → Bookmarks.
onboarding.statusMonitorTruncatedNote: Showing {shown} of {total} bookmarks across all pages. Enable more per bookmark in config → Bookmarks.
onboarding.statusMonitorGithubHint: Good example — pings reliably and shows how status dots work.
onboarding.bookmarksInputStepBody: Arrow keys move the highlight; Enter or Space opens; semicolon (;) edits. Drag the left strip to reorder; press and hold a row (not the strip) for about half a second for inline edit; press and hold a category title the same way to rename it. More in Help → Dashboard bookmarks.
onboarding.finishBodyReady: Setup complete. You can change anything later in config. Keyboard and mouse bookmark tips are in Help → Dashboard bookmarks.
onboarding.finishBodyStart: Setup complete. You have {count} page(s) — organize them in config → Pages. Press + for the full bookmark form, or & for a quick add. Keyboard and mouse tips are in Help → Dashboard bookmarks.

featureTour.step1Body: Discover the most powerful features in a few clicks. You can always skip the tour or restart it later via Config.
featureTour.step2Body: Press ":" or click this button. Change theme with :theme dark, adjust columns with :columns 4, or add a bookmark with :new. Commands are grouped and searchable.
featureTour.step3Body: Press "?" to open your finders. Finders are shortcuts to search engines. A DuckDuckGo finder is ready by default — type "?du linux" to search directly. Add or remove your own finders via Config → Finders.
featureTour.step4Body: Press ">" or click the search button. Use filters like status:online, category:work or tag:dev. Your search history and saved searches are always available.
featureTour.step5Body: Set the number of columns that fits your screen. Favicons are the website icons next to each bookmark — handy for quick recognition.
featureTour.step5ShowIconsHint: Website icons next to each bookmark for quick recognition.
featureTour.step6Body: nextDash automatically groups your bookmarks into dynamic sections. The Today collection shows bookmarks fitting your time of day: work tools in the morning, relaxation in the evening.
featureTour.step6TodayHint: Shows bookmarks that fit your time of day.
featureTour.step6MostUsedHint: Shows your most opened bookmarks in one overview.
featureTour.step7Body: Use arrow keys to navigate, Enter to open and ; to edit inline. Drag via the narrow handle strip on the left to reorder. In Config → Bookmarks you manage everything in bulk, import and export.
featureTour.step8Body: The tour is complete. All features are fully configurable via Config: themes, layout version (Classic, Modern, or Glass), layout presets, finders, smart collections and bookmark management.

postTuning.languageBody: Pick the language for the dashboard and config. You can change this anytime under Config → General.
postTuning.themeBody: Choose a starting theme. Customize colors later under Config → theme.
postTuning.extensionBody: Install the nextDash browser extension to add the current tab as a bookmark without leaving the page.
